top_story: A fragile U.S.-Iran de-escalation collapsed on 26 June when Washington struck Iranian missile, drone, and coastal radar sites after accusing Tehran of attacking a commercial cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran framed the strikes as a breach of the recent peace deal and answered with attacks on U.S. targets in the Gulf, turning a maritime security incident into a direct bilateral exchange. The choice of coastal military targets shows a U.S. effort to blunt Iran’s capacity to threaten shipping, but it also pushes the confrontation closer to densely trafficked sea lanes that anchor Gulf economies. The immediate takeaway is that the diplomatic floor has given way, leaving commercial navigation and civilian confidence exposed to rapid further escalation.
